name: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS
notes: The paper calls this the first search for new physics performed with the ICARUS detector at Fermilab; it uses the off-axis NuMI beam rather than the on-axis BNB beam used for the sterile-neutrino search.

significance.locator: arXiv:2411.02727, abstract (no significance/sigma reported for a null result)
significance.note: An exclusion-limit search: no signal was observed.

summary.plain: ICARUS searched for a hidden-sector particle that could be produced in kaon decays and then decay into two muons inside the detector. It saw no signal and set limits; the paper describes them as world-leading for heavy QCD axions and, among dedicated searches, for the Higgs portal scalar.
summary.technical: Search for long-lived particles from K → π + S decays with S → μ+μ− inside ICARUS-T600, using 2.41×10^20 POT from the NuMI beam at Fermilab. No new physics signal is observed; the paper sets world-leading limits on heavy QCD axions, as well as for the Higgs portal scalar among dedicated searches, and presents limits in a model-independent way applicable to any model predicting K → π + S(→ μμ) with a long-lived S.

title: Search for a Hidden Sector Scalar from Kaon Decay in the Di-Muon Final State at ICARUS
why_it_matters: The paper calls this the first search for new physics performed with the ICARUS detector at Fermilab, and says it paves the way for the future program of long-lived particle searches at ICARUS. The channel would be a signal of hidden-sector models that can address the strong CP problem and the microphysical origin of dark matter.
